Cc: ops@terminus.ai, priya.shah@terminus.ai
Date: 2026-07-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden p95 spikes + 5xx after v2.1 deploy

Hi Kimberly —

We rolled Terminus AI v2.1 (quant profile qv2-light) last night and immediately started seeing p95 latency jump from ~220ms to ~780ms and a 3% 5xx error rate across our inference endpoints. Throughput has dropped ~18% for our high-concurrency routes. This started at ~01:30 PDT and is still ongoing.

Attached are a small sample of request payloads and server-side traces (we redacted keys). Can you confirm whether Redwood made any runtime/kernel changes tied to the new quant profile selection? This is impacting checkout flows — our ops team is escalating to the CTO and requesting an immediate rollback if there isn’t a safe mitigation.

We need an exec-level bridge within the hour. Please advise next steps and who from Redwood will join.

Thanks,
Alex Navarro
Head of Platform — Terminus.ai

- Kick off an executive bridge (30 min) so we have product, eng, infra, and your ops in the same call. Marissa will schedule.
- Engineering triage: Dylan is starting a live diff between qv2-light and qv2-stable kernel plans; initial ask is to capture kernel-level timings and KV-cache miss rates.
- Short-term mitigation: we can pin your routes to qv2-stable or roll the model back to the prior model build if we confirm the profile is causing the regression.

I’ll loop in Rishi for any exec-level remediation/credits. Please stand by for a calendar invite in 10 minutes.

—Kimberly Park

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai

Date: 2026-07-15T10:01:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Sudden p95 spikes + 5xx after v2.1 deploy — preliminary triage

Quick triage notes (initial, from infra metrics):

- The qv2-light path introduced a different matmul kernel selection on A100 Gen2 that increases per-token latency for sequences > 256 in our microbench.
- KV cache miss ratio for Terminus traffic spiked ~11% vs baseline, likely because the quantization layout changed memory access patterns.
- Aggregate p95 on the serving pool shows CPU spike in relay layer at ~01:32 PDT and decoder stalls consistent with cache thrash.

Actionable items:
- Immediate: Recommend pinning Terminus routes to qv2-stable across the serving pool. This is a config flip and should take < 15 minutes to roll out to their production pool with 2m staggered batches.
- Medium: We'll produce a microkernel patch to address the kernel choice (non-trivial) and run a small canary.

I’ve started a hotfix branch and collected the kernel traces (referenced in the Drive link). If Kimberly approves, I’ll push the pin now and monitor telemetry.

—Dylan Brooks
Senior SRE — Serving Runtime
